texts: The bell teaches that it speaks only when struck, the mountain that it stands unmoved; a humble heart learns from both
hey can u write something on learning from a bell and a mountain, every little thing teaches
bell, mountain, learning from all
I need a doha about the wise learner who takes a lesson from the ringing of a bell and the stillness of a mountain, never too proud to learn from the ordinary things of the world around him
on our trek, the quiet peak and the distant bell of a goat taught my son more about patience than his school had in a year
At the crossroads a thorn pricked the wanderer, and he learned more from that small hurt than from all his books
I once stepped on a thorn at a crossroads in the village and my grandfather said that was today's teacher, and he was right
crossroads, thorn, lesson
doha on learning from a thorn at the crossroads, life teaches everywhere

Can you shape a verse about the one who learns from everything he meets, even from a thorn lying at the crossroads, taking its lesson of caution and care, since any humble teacher can teach one who is ready
my daughter watched the moon change over a month and came to me asking about patience and loss, she learned it before I could teach her
doha on how even the moon can be a teacher
Write a doha about the wise one who learns from all creation, who sees in the moon the lesson of change, in the humble and the great alike a teacher, and who therefore never stops growing wiser
moon, a teacher
The moon teaches waxing and waning without a word, and the humble heart learns the way of the world from it

Give me a doha on learning from a humble bridge, which carries rich and poor alike across without discrimination, and teaches without speaking the lesson of serving every person and asking nothing in return
The bridge bears all who cross and asks no fare; learn from it, O wise one, the art of giving without a name
every day I cross the old bridge on the way to work, and lately I've realised it teaches me to carry others over without asking for anything
what can i learn from a bridge, crossing over like it teaches
bridge, lesson
I learned patience from the priest at our colony and honesty from the vegetable seller, and my mother says a wise person learns from everyone
priest, learn from all
From the priest take his prayer, from the child his joy, from every soul one lesson, and grow rich

I need a doha about the wise learner who sits before a priest to learn devotion but also takes lessons from a child, a farmer and a stranger, understanding that wisdom is scattered everywhere for those who look
doha on learning something from a priest and from everyone else too
Take the thief's patience and his watchfulness, and leave his deed; the wise find a lesson in every corner
a reformed thief who sweeps our street told me about patience and being awake at night, and I realised I could learn from anyone
Write a doha about the wise one who finds a lesson even in a thief, taking his alertness, his patience and his daring, and leaving his crime behind, since the good may be gathered from any teacher
doha on learning from a thief, even he has a lesson
thief, a lesson

Looking for a doha about learning from the humble shroud, which teaches that nothing can be carried beyond this life, and the one who learns this lesson early can live simply and freely without regret
The shroud has no pockets, and that is its lesson; the wise learn it before they need it
what can i learn from a shroud, it teaches u what matters
shroud, lesson
I saw a plain white shroud being carried to the burning ground and for the first time I understood what my teacher meant about owning less
got a doha on what a date palm teaches, it gives fruit only high up?
Give me a doha on learning from the date palm that grows tall and bears sweet fruit only after many years, a quiet teacher for those who watch and listen without hurrying
date palm, wise lesson
an old date palm outside our home taught me patience, because it only bore fruit after years of waiting, and my grandfather said that was a lesson
The date palm stands tall but gives its sweetness only to those who reach; learn from it the cost of height
my mother can't read or write, but I've learned more about running a household and treating people from her than from any teacher or any course
Not only from the learned, not only from the great; the wise child learns from the lowly and grows

Write a doha about learning from every humble teacher, from the servant, the child and the simple villager, who each carry a lesson that the proud scholar misses, and who teach without ever knowing they do
doha on learning from simple humble people
learn from the humble
cotton, needle, lesson
Can you shape a verse about the lessons hidden in cotton and a needle, the one soft and yielding, the other sharp and joining, both teaching the wise learner to unite what is torn
my grandmother taught me more about life by threading a needle and spinning cotton than any lecture I ever sat through
what can i learn from cotton and a needle
The needle pierces only to join, the cotton yields to be made into cloth; from both the wise learn their trade
my father says every person he has met taught him something, even the ones who behaved badly taught him what not to do
Gather the good from every garden, and you will need no orchard of your own

Looking for a doha about the wise one who takes whatever is good from whoever he meets, ignoring the faults and the failings, so that his wisdom grows from a thousand teachers who never thought of themselves as teachers
take good, leave rest
doha on picking up good things from everyone around u
swan, mosque, learning
a swan was gliding near the mosque as the call to prayer sounded, and it seemed to my grandfather like a lesson on taking the best of everything
Write a doha about the wise learner who, like the swan, takes only the good from everywhere he goes, from the mosque and from the busy lanes, from the old and from the young, leaving the rest
doha on a swan taking the good from the mosque and everywhere
The swan takes the cream from the water and the wise take wisdom from the mosque, the field and the road alike
a jeweller friend showed me how gold doesn't tarnish, and I realised it taught him patience in a way no person ever did
gold, a lesson
Gold is tested by heat and does not fade; the wise learn from it the way of enduring
I need a doha about the wise learner who watches gold and what it teaches, that true worth does not rust or change in hard times, a silent lesson for those who care to observe the world around them
what can i learn from gold, what it teaches
I watched a bee gather from the dew on the garden flowers one morning, and my teacher said that was a better lesson than any class
dew, bee, lessons
The dew teaches how to be brief, the bee how to gather; from small things the wise learn the greatest
doha on learning from dew and a bee

Can you shape a verse about the lessons of the small, the morning dew that vanishes without complaint and the bee that gathers sweetness patiently, which the wise watch, take to heart, and use in their own lives

Write a doha about learning from the scales that weigh everything honestly, without regard for who stands before them, a humble teacher of fairness for those who observe the shopkeepers and their daily work
I watched the grain seller at the scales and learned how a poor man can stay fair with everyone, more than I learned in my ethics class
scales, a lesson
doha on learning from the scales, what fairness teaches
The scales hold no favourites; learn from them how to weigh without bias and speak without fear
sword, a lesson
what can i learn from a sword, what it teaches u
my uncle, a retired soldier, used to say his sword was his best teacher because it taught him control and the weight of his actions
The sword teaches that sharpness without wisdom wounds; learn from it the restraint that the swordsman learns
Give me a doha on learning from the sword, a teacher of discipline and restraint, whose power is meaningful only in the hand of someone who has learned when not to use it
In the house the loom clacks a lesson: strand by strand the cloth is made, and patience is the weaver's teacher
doha on learning from a loom in the house
growing up in a house with a loom in the front room, I picked up patience and care simply by watching my father work it
loom, house, lesson

I need a doha about learning from the loom in the house, a quiet teacher of patience and pattern, from which every careful watcher takes the lesson of building something bigger one small piece at a time

Compose a doha about learning from a mirror that shows the truth about oneself and a spinning wheel that teaches steady patience, both humble household objects that carry lessons for anyone willing to learn
doha on learning from a mirror and a spinning wheel
mirror, spinning wheel, lessons
my grandmother's spinning wheel and her small mirror sit side by side, and between them I learned both to be patient and to see my own faults
The mirror teaches honesty and the spinning wheel teaches patience; the wise find a teacher in each common thing
The beggar teaches humility and the value of a small gift; the wise sit beside him and learn
a beggar near our station thanked me so deeply for a bit of bread that I realised how little I thank anyone for anything

Looking for a doha about learning from a beggar, who knows what the rich have forgotten, gratitude and contentment with little, a teacher of the heart sitting quietly by the roadside for those who care to learn
what can i learn from a beggar
beggar, a lesson
Give me a doha on learning from the peacock, which shows how to enjoy beauty and joy while remaining humble about one's own flaws, a living teacher for those who watch nature with an open mind
doha on learning from a peacock
a peacock in the courtyard of my college taught me that even the most beautiful thing has its flaws, and that we should look at ourselves honestly
peacock, a lesson
The peacock dances in joy and looks down at his feet; the wise learn from him both delight and humility
doha on a spinning wheel teaching u something
my mother turned the spinning wheel every evening without hurry, and I learned from her that slow and steady work builds something lasting
The spinning wheel turns, the yarn grows, and from its small round the wise learn the long work of life
spinning wheel, a teacher

Compose a doha about learning from a spinning wheel, whose steady turning teaches patience and the value of small daily effort, a gentle teacher in an ordinary household for the one who has eyes to see
palace, a lesson

Can you shape a verse about learning from an old palace, grand once and now falling silent, which teaches the wise visitor about the passing of power and the value of simple things, if he is willing to listen
The palace teaches that all that is high must someday fall; the wise read its ruins as a book
visiting the ruined palace on our school trip, our teacher said the ruins taught more than all the textbooks about how things do not last
what can i learn from a palace, what kings forget
inn, priest, lessons
The inn teaches that all are guests; the priest teaches that all are equal; the wise learn from both
at the inn on the highway the priest and the cook sat side by side eating, and I learned something about equality that I never forgot

Looking for a doha about learning from the inn that welcomes every guest alike and from the priest who sits there with the rest, a lesson about humility and equality that any wanderer may carry on his way
doha on learning from an inn and a priest
temple, learning

Write a doha about learning at the temple, not only from the sermon but from the humble people there, the sweeper, the devotee, and the child, each one carrying a lesson for one who is ready to receive
doha on learning something good at a temple, from anyone
At the temple the wise learn not only from the sermon but from the sweeper, the stranger and the child
I went to the temple every week with my grandmother, and the lesson I remember most is how she greeted every person there as if they mattered
crossroads, a lesson
The crossroads teaches choice and consequence; the wise stand and watch before they walk
standing at a crossroads in the old town, I watched people choose and realised that every choice carries its own lesson
I need a doha about learning from a crossroads, which shows that every road is a choice and every choice has a result, a silent teacher in the heart of every village for those who stop to look
what can i learn from a crossroads, every road teaches
I learned more about people from watching the vegetable market on Sundays than I did in my psychology course
doha on learning from a market, so many teachers
market, teachers everywhere

Can you shape a verse about learning from the market, where every seller, every buyer and every passerby is a teacher of human nature, and the wise learner walks through it with open eyes and a quiet mind
The market is a school without walls; every seller is a teacher and every buyer a lesson
doha on learning from anyone and everyone
The wise drink from every cup and are thirsty still; they bow to each who has something to give
everyone is a teacher
my father says he learned from his barber, his driver and his neighbour's child as much as from his professors
Write a doha about the wise one who bows to every person he meets, knowing each carries a lesson he lacks, the lowly as much as the learned, and so he grows every day
what can i learn from a physician and jaggery
Give me a doha on learning from the physician who gives bitter medicine and from the jaggery that sweetens it, a pair of humble teachers showing the wise how to be both honest and kind
our family physician mixed jaggery in a bitter tonic and taught me how to make hard things easy for others to swallow
physician, jaggery, lessons
The physician teaches that bitter cures and sweet delights, and the jaggery that sweetness is simple; the wise learn both
The wise child gathers from joy and from sorrow alike, and finds that both were teachers
my failed business taught me more about people and money than my successful one ever did, and I'm thankful to it now
every experience teaches
doha on learning from every experience, good or bad

I need a doha about learning from every experience, the pleasant and the painful, the successful and the broken, for the wise find a teacher in every event and grow in understanding with each passing year
a traveler stayed at our home one night and told us about people in distant towns, and I learned more about the world from him than from my books
A traveler stops for a night and gives a lesson; the wise listen to each stranger as to a master
Write a doha about learning from the traveler who passes through, carrying the stories and the wisdom of the road, and the wise host who listens with respect to everything the stranger has to offer
doha on learning from a traveler passing by
traveler, a lesson
what can i learn from a skeleton, bones teach too
in our biology lab the old skeleton taught me more about how alike we all are than any of my lessons on equality
The skeleton has no title and no rank, and in its silence it teaches all that matters; the wise take notice
skeleton, a lesson
Looking for a doha about learning from a skeleton, which stripped of skin and rank teaches that all humans are the same beneath, a silent teacher for anyone who looks at it with an honest mind
doha on learning from a palace guard
Give me a doha on learning from the humble gatekeeper of a palace, who watches kings and ministers all day and understands human nature better than any scholar, if only the wise will sit and listen
The doorkeeper of the palace knows more of kings than the courtiers, and the wise ask him
palace, humble teacher
the guard at the palace gate told us stories about the royal family that taught me more about power than I ever learned in history class
at the zoo I watched a lion rest calmly while the crowd made noise, and it taught me that strength doesn't need to shout
lion, a lesson
doha on learning courage from a lion
Compose a doha about learning from the lion, king of the wild, who rests quietly and strikes only when needed, a living lesson in strength and restraint for the wise observer
The lion teaches that real strength is quiet; the wise watch him and learn when not to roar
net, moon, lessons
what can i learn from a net and the moon
a fisherman mending his net under the moon told me stories about patience that I could not find in any book
The net teaches that gathering holds only what is caught, the moon that sharing lights all; the wise learn from both
Can you shape a verse about learning from a fisherman's net and the moon above it, each teaching the wise watcher a different lesson, one about careful labour and the other about generous light
a small kindness from a stranger on a bad day taught me more than a year of lectures
small things teach
doha on learning from small things

Looking for a doha about the wise one who learns from small and humble things, a word, a gesture, a passing sight, understanding that great lessons are often hidden in the most ordinary moments of the day
The smallest grain teaches the whole its beginning; the wise learn big things from small
a snake in the field behind our gold-seller's home taught me caution and a lesson about greed, according to my uncle
The snake teaches caution, gold the cost of greed; the wise learn from both and walk gently
doha on learning from gold and a snake
Write a doha about learning from the snake, which strikes only when disturbed, and from gold, which tempts the greedy, two silent teachers who show the wise how to move through the world with care
gold, snake, lessons
river, a lesson
I grew up beside a river and learned from it how to keep moving, how to go around obstacles, and how to let things pass
what can i learn from a river

I need a doha about learning from the river, which moves around every obstacle without complaint and gives itself to the fields and the thirsty, a teacher of flow and generosity for those who sit beside it
The river teaches that to give is to flow, and to flow is to reach the sea; the wise follow its example

Can you shape a verse about learning from children, who laugh freely and forgive at once and ask questions without shame, small teachers in every household for a grown-up who has not forgotten how to listen
learn from children
The child teaches wonder, the elder patience, the stranger kindness; the wise bow to all three
doha on learning from children
my five-year-old forgave her friend in two minutes after a big quarrel, and I realised how much I still had to learn from her
doha on learning from the sand, humble teacher
sand, a lesson
walking on the beach with my teacher, he told me to notice how the sand takes every footprint and lets the waves smooth it, and called that forgiveness
Compose a doha about the lesson of sand, which takes every footprint without complaint and lets the wind smooth it away, a quiet teacher of forgiveness and yielding for the wise who walk upon it
The sand holds no shape of its own and takes every footprint; the wise learn from it how to yield
what can i learn from a lotus at a crossroads
The lotus blooms in mud and stays clean; the crossroads shows the many ways; the wise learn from both
crossroads, lotus, lessons
a lotus blooming in a muddy pond by the crossroads in our village taught me that beauty can grow from anything, and I think of it whenever I am down
Give me a doha on learning from the lotus that rises from mud unstained and from the crossroads where all paths meet, two humble teachers showing the wise how to stay pure while choosing the way
doha on learning from a fly and a moneylender
fly, moneylender, lessons

I need a doha about learning from the fly caught in sweetness and the moneylender caught in his accounts, two small and unlikely teachers who show the wise learner how easily greed and appetite can trap us
The fly teaches that sweetness can trap; the moneylender that debt can bind; the wise learn from the small and the stern
a fly drowned in my sweet tea while the moneylender in our lane was demanding payment, and I got two lessons about greed in one afternoon
The shadow follows the one who flees it and flees the one who follows; the traveler learns this on the road
a traveler resting in the shadow of a wall told me something about patience that I remember to this day
shadow, traveler, lessons
doha on learning from a shadow and a traveler

Write a doha about the lesson of the shadow, which follows the traveler wherever he goes and cannot be escaped, and which the wise traveler learns to accept and to walk with as a quiet teacher on the road
what can i learn from a cloud and an oil press
cloud, oil press, lessons

Looking for a doha about learning from the passing cloud that gives rain and moves on and from the oil press that gives its oil and asks for nothing, two humble teachers of generosity for the wise to observe
The cloud gives water and drifts away, the oil press gives oil and keeps the husk; the wise learn generosity from both
we visited an oil press under a rain cloud and the old pressman taught us about giving what you have and asking nothing back
The lotus teaches how to live in the world without being stained by it; the wise learn from it in silence
lotus, a lesson
Give me a doha on learning from the lotus that rises above the mud and stays clean, a quiet teacher of detachment and purity, for the person who looks at it with attention and an open heart
a single lotus floating in the pond behind our school taught me something about staying clean in a dirty place, and I never forgot it
doha on learning from a lotus
doha on learning from everyday life
Each day is a school and each hour a lesson; the wise are those who enrol and attend

Compose a doha about learning from the everyday events of ordinary life, the quarrel, the kindness, the delay and the surprise, each of which carries a lesson for those who pay attention and do not rush past
everyday wisdom
my mother learned more from running our home through hardship than any college could have taught her, and she passes all of it on
everyone teaches
Not one soul is empty of a lesson; the wise go through the world as a student goes through a school
Can you shape a verse about the wise one who believes every person has something to teach him, who listens to the lowly and the learned alike, and gathers a little from all and so becomes full
my grandfather listened to his gardener and his cook as closely as to a professor, and he was always the wisest man in the room
doha on how everyone has something to teach
I watched a fish in a still pond swim in perfect ease, and it taught me what it means to accept my situation
Looking for a doha about learning from the fish, which lives in water without struggle and moves with the current, a gentle lesson in acceptance for those who spend long hours watching a pond
The fish teaches how to live in what surrounds you and not to fight the stream; the wise learn from it
doha on learning from a fish
fish, a lesson
doha on learning from a shadow
Write a doha about learning from a shadow, which grows and shrinks through the day, a humble teacher of change and of time for the one who watches and does not take the passing hours for granted
shadow, a lesson
my grandfather read time from the shadow of a pole in the yard, and told me that watching it taught him patience
The shadow teaches that nothing stays the same through the day; the wise watch it and understand time
doha on a net and a blind man teaching us
The blind man mends his net by touch, and the seeing learn from his patience what eyes can never show
I need a doha about learning from the blind man who mends his net by touch alone, a humble teacher of patience and attention, whose lesson is plain to anyone willing to sit beside him and watch
a blind man in our village mends fishing nets with his hands, and I learned from him that you do not need sight to do good work
net, blind man, lessons
watching an elephant walk through a noisy crowd without a care taught me how little I need to react to everything
Can you shape a verse about learning from the elephant who walks calmly past the barking dogs, a gentle teacher of poise and patience for anyone who watches with a respectful mind and a quiet heart
doha on learning from an elephant
The elephant walks on while the dogs bark; the wise learn from him the dignity of calm
elephant, a lesson
